findings.title: Global obstacle representation fails even for natural boundary data

locators: Proposition 8.2 → Theorem 2.5 proof dependence (parent-read later-section check)
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.claim: For every admissible boundary value on an arbitrary bounded Lipschitz Ω, the variational upper obstacle M equals min_{w∈∂Ω}(h_N(z−w)+h0(w)), and likewise for the lower obstacle.

counterexample.domain: Ω=((−2,2)×(−1,1)) ∪ ((−2,−1)×(0,3)) ∪ ((1,2)×(0,3)). This is a bounded simply connected Lipschitz U-shaped polygon.
counterexample.function: Set a(x)=1 for x≤−1, a(x)=−x for −1≤x≤1, and a(x)=−1 for x≥1. Define u(x,y)=a(x)y and h0=u|∂Ω.
counterexample.admissibility_proof: On either arm, ∇u=(0,±1). In the middle strip −1<x<1, the domain has |y|<1 and ∇u=(−y,−x). Hence ∇u∈[−1,1]² a.e. The same formula extends to the enclosing rectangle and obeys |u(x,y)−u(x',y')|≤3|x−x'|+|y−y'|, so u∈C^{0,1}(closure Ω) and h0 is Lipschitz. Thus A_N is nonempty exactly under (3.17).
counterexample.evaluation: At z=(−3/2,5/2), u(z)=5/2, so the true upper obstacle defined by (3.22) is at least 5/2. At boundary w=(1,3), h0(w)=−3 and h_N(z−w)=|−5/2|+|−1/2|=3. The right side of (3.23) is therefore ≤0. The two purportedly equal quantities differ by at least 5/2.
counterexample.additional_boundary_check: At z_b=(−1,3), h0(z_b)=3, but choosing w=(1,3) in the formula gives at most −1. Thus the formula does not even recover this admissible boundary trace.
counterexample.surface_tension_compatibility: The obstacle assertion depends only on N, Ω and h0. The article's existence statement for (3.1) permits the square with convex affine boundary data, for example L=0 and no gas masses; the example is not excluded by the surface-tension class.

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.mechanism: A local gradient constraint on a nonconvex domain controls differences along paths inside the domain. It does not impose the direct whole-plane support-distance inequality across a gap in the domain.
counterevidence_and_repairs: The variational definitions (3.22) remain meaningful and valid; the counterexample targets their identification with (3.23).

Convex Ω makes the direct segment argument applicable. Another sufficient condition is global h_N-Lipschitz compatibility of the boundary data. On a nonconvex domain with this extra boundary condition, use the final interior segment ending at z and boundary compatibility along the remaining collinear displacement.

For the general locally constrained class, the appropriate candidate formula uses the intrinsic directed path distance generated by h_N inside the domain. This is a change to the formula, not a condition already present in (3.17).

The original u witness was not asserted natural. The strengthened v witness is proved natural by the actual definitions, so the failed identity reaches the class used in Proposition 8.2. Neither witness is claimed oriented, and neither disproves Proposition 8.2's piecewise-affine conclusion or Theorem 2.5.

The parent actually read the later proofs and supplied local replacements for the needed bounds in Lemma 7.1/Theorem 7.3 and for the competitor in Theorem 8.1. Those checks are separately attributed in parent_dependency_update.json. The global identification used in Proposition 8.2 remains unjustified; an intrinsic-distance repair has not been established.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.dependency_assessment: The identity is false inside the natural-data class, and the parent traced its use in the central piecewise-affine obstacle argument Proposition 8.2 → Theorem 2.5. This is a material proof gap, not a proved false conclusion of either theorem. The absence of a counterexample to their conclusions does not validate the proof; the proposed intrinsic polyhedral-distance replacement still requires proof.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.severity: Major (recommended on current proof dependence): a false representation is used for a central structural result within its actual hypothesis class. The grade is not based on repair length. No main-theorem counterexample is claimed.

strengthened_natural_counterexample.origin: This helper derived the modification while reassessing scientific dependence. The parent then reported a concurrent independent derivation of the same trace with an additive constant +2. Both are internal native current checks; neither is independent acceptance.
strengthened_natural_counterexample.function: Retain Ω, N and a(x) from the original witness. Set b(x)=x+1 for x≤−1, b(x)=0 for |x|≤1, and b(x)=x−1 for x≥1; define v(x,y)=a(x)y+b(x), h0=v|∂Ω.
strengthened_natural_counterexample.admissibility: On the left arm ∇v=(1,1), on the right arm ∇v=(1,−1), and in the central strip ∇v=(−y,−x), with |x|,|y|<1. Thus ∇v∈N a.e. The formula extends continuously to the enclosing rectangle and obeys |Δv|≤4|Δx|+|Δy|, so v∈C^{0,1}(closure Ω).
strengthened_natural_counterexample.natural_data_proof: Each boundary side is affine. At every polygon corner the two incident affine slopes equal the two components of the displayed assigned corner p_n of N. Every corner assignment satisfies either the pair (3.31) or the pair (3.32), as verified by exact zero dot products; the same assignments satisfy the full affine trace condition (3.33) on both incident sides. No relation between assignments at neighboring Ω corners is required, as the source explicitly notes on printed 371. Hence Ω and h0 meet Definitions 3.8–3.9.
strengthened_natural_counterexample.decisive_values: At z=(−3/2,5/2), v(z)=2, so the true M(z)≥2. At w=(1,3), h0(w)=−3 and h_N(z−w)=3, so (3.23) gives at most 0. At z_b=(−1,3), h0(z_b)=3 but the same boundary formula gives at most −1.
strengthened_natural_counterexample.scope: This disproves the global obstacle identification even for natural boundary data on a natural simply connected nonconvex domain. Oriented boundary data in Definition 7.2 are not claimed. It is not a counterexample to the conclusion of Proposition 8.2, Theorem 2.5, Theorem 8.3 or the main universality theorem.

findings.severity_reason: The false whole-plane representation is used in a central structural proof within its actual natural-data hypothesis class. Adjacent local repairs do not supply the unresolved global representation; conclusions of Proposition8.2 and Theorem2.5 are not themselves disproved.

findings.title: Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.origin: Parent supplied b, γ and g as a candidate. This helper independently checked the equation, boundary hypotheses, homeomorphism, exact ray algebra and actual printed source pages. This is supplemental internal checking, not independent acceptance.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.claim: At a simple cusp, the images of both exact original-disc straight rays z0−t z0 exp(±iπ/6) are asymptotic to the line orthogonal to the cusp tangent.

counterexample.representation_check: (γ−b·overline(γ))/(1−|b|²) has numerator (1−r)[z(1+r)+z²] and denominator (1−r)(1+r+r²), giving the stated g in D.
counterexample.equation_check: g_z=[1+2r+(2+r)z]/D². Direct differentiation gives g_barz=−z³[1+2r+(2+r)bar z]/D²=−b(z)·overline(g_z). Thus the image-confirmed equation (5.17) holds.
counterexample.regularity_and_boundedness: D≥1 for r≥0, so g is real analytic on C and bounded on the closed unit disk; in particular it is a bounded W^{1,2}_loc solution. b is analytic, |b|<1 in D and |b|→1 at every point of the unit circle.
counterexample.jacobian_check: A zero of g_z in the closed disk would require z=−s real, 0≤s≤1, with s(2+s²)=1+2s². This is (s−1)(s²−s+1)=0, whose only real solution in that range is s=1. Consequently g_z≠0 in D and J_g=(1−|z|⁶)|g_z|²>0 there.
counterexample.boundary_and_homeomorphism: On |z|=1, g(z)=R(z)=(2z+z²)/3. If R(z1)=R(z2), then (z1−z2)(z1+z2+2)=0; distinct closed-disk points cannot have sum −2. Thus R is univalent in D and injective on its boundary, giving a positively oriented Jordan cardioid. Since g has the same continuous boundary map and positive local degree inside, its degree is one for points in the cardioid interior and zero outside. Each interior point therefore has exactly one preimage, no outside point has a preimage, and openness excludes interior points mapping onto the boundary. Hence g is a homeomorphism onto the bounded cardioid interior.
counterexample.cusp_check: At z0=−1, R'(z0)=0 and R''(z0)=2/3≠0, while R(−e^{is})+1/3=−s²/3−i s³/3+O(s⁴). Thus w0=−1/3 is a simple cusp whose tangent line is real.
counterexample.exact_ray_identity: For a=e^{iθ}, c=cos θ and z=−1+t a, D=3−6ct+(4c²+3)t²−4ct³+t⁴ and g(z)+1/3=[(4c²−3)t²+(3a−4c)t³+t⁴]/(3D). This follows by direct polynomial expansion; no numerical approximation is used.
counterexample.decisive_expansion: At θ=±π/6, g(−1+t e^{±iπ/6})+1/3=[(−√3±3i)/18]t³+O(t⁴). The nonzero real component makes the limiting line nonorthogonal to the real cusp tangent. The two limiting transverse lines also differ from one another.

counterevidence_and_scope: The stated O(t³) estimate in (5.35) holds for this example, with a nonzero cubic coefficient.
For every other inward angle in the corollary, the displayed exact identity has nonzero real quadratic coefficient (4cos²θ−3)/9. Thus the general quadratic behavior in part (i) also survives.

A Möbius change from the original disk to a half-plane does not carry these exact straight rays to exact straight rays: a second-order path displacement can modify the cubic coefficient when the quadratic leading term cancels.

The example proves failure of the perpendicular-direction clause in Corollary 5.17(ii). It does not disprove the main Hölder exponents, the Pokrovsky–Talapov law, general transversality, or the universality theorem.
Which later statements require exact orthogonality rather than cubic order or mere transversality remains a parent proof-dependency check.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.severity: Minor (recommended for the localized exact-direction refinement): the explicit example preserves cubic compression, transversality and the other quadratic directions. No failure of a central rate theorem is inferred; the parent retains final proof-dependency assessment.

findings.severity_reason: A localized exact-direction clause has an explicit admissible teleomorphic counterexample. Cubic compression,transversality,other quadratic directions and later exponent arguments survive; no central rate or universality failure inferred.
